title: Toyota’s Crown Signia GT-S Embraces Station-Wagon Swagger

body_markdown:
It’s been a whopping 30 years since Toyota released the first[RAV4](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-2026-toyota-rav4-adds-power-looks-and-gr-flair/) in America, a vehicle that’s arguably the first modern crossover utility vehicle (CUV). Last year, Toyota launched the posh[Crown Signia crossover utility](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-toyota-crown-signia-limited-old-name-new-look-old-soul/) , which both replaced the Venza and gave Toyota a vehicle that skirts the boundaries of a station wagon. But while the Signia isn’t the successor to the 1987 Toyota Cressida station wagon, it’s called the Crown Estate in markets outside of North America for ample reason. That rationale is amplified with the Crown GT-S Concept, a vehicle made for the 2026 Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) trade show.


This concept was built by the Toyota Motorsports Garage, a skunkworks group responsible for[previous SEMA builds](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/nascar-powered-land-cruiser-proves-toyota-sees-into-americas-soul-now/) that highlighted the potential of Toyota’s trucks, sports cars, and perhaps even station wagons. Toyota suggests the Crown Signia GT-S Concept is a “sleek grand touring machine that blends everyday space and comfort with the attitude and road feel of a true sports car.” As with many skunkworks initiatives aimed at the automotive aftermarket, the revised hardware likely proves the point.


Toyota


Toyota


Toyota gave this wagon a set of aftermarket lowering coilovers, which drop the body a full five inches. This is probably the most important part, because in many ways the Crown Signia GT-S Concept is less of a crossover and more of a wagon. As per usual, the lowered stance includes upgraded wheels, in this case 21-inch HREs with 295mm-wide tires that give the GT-S a 20% larger footprint over a stock Crown Signia. Brakes were also sized up for the wheels, borrowed from the upscale Lexus RX 500h F-Sport.


Toyota


Toyota


Toyota


Body modifications continue the Crown Signia’s transformation into a wagon, as wide-body fenders pair well with the long roof. Red trim accents give this Toyota a turbocharged 1980s vibe, the front fenders have integral vents, and the rear sports a custom exhaust. A body kit visually lowers the package and connects both fascias together in a manner befitting a flagship performance touring vehicle. Interior modifications include new bucket seats with the GT-S logo on the headrests.


Toyota


Toyota


Those headrests are a nice throwback to the Celica GT-S and its performance enhancements over a stock Celica coupe. While Toyota provides no information about whether the concept’s powertrain has been enhanced over the regular version, the Crown Signia GT-S proves that a mere crossover can become a station wagon with the tricks and trade normally found in a SEMA custom car.


Adding the turbocharged Hybrid Max powertrain in a production GT-S version would be the icing on this conceptual cake. But even as it stands, the standard 240-hp driveline that returns 38 miles per gallon is precisely what’s needed in such a practical vehicle. No matter what happens after this year’s SEMA show, Toyota would be wise to implement some of the GT-S Concept’s swagger back into a production model. Because the more station wagons we can get back into our automotive ecosystem, the better car culture becomes.
